summary.title: Software Engineering - The Soft Parts
summary.one_liner: Addy Osmani's reflections from ten years on Google Chrome on the non-coding skills that help engineers grow: critical thinking, fundamentals, user focus, managing complexity, and design docs.
keywords: jack of all trades vs specialist
mastery high value shipped per hour
takeaways: Critical thinking means asking whether you solve the right problem, finding root causes, and testing whether evidence supports conclusions.
Learn macro fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, architecture) because they transfer across languages, while micro details like frameworks change.
Choose proven ('boring') technology for new projects and only adopt new tools when they add real value; use side projects to explore new tech.
Keep code specific to the problem but slightly generic where cheap; favor deep modules with small, simple interfaces.
Write design docs as an integral part of engineering to gather feedback, record decisions, and help future team members.
summary.summary: This long-form essay by Addy Osmani shares soft-skill lessons from his first decade on Google Chrome, organized into sections on learning, mastery, critical thinking, fundamentals, user focus, upgrading skills, technical complexity, legacy and green-field projects, debugging, and design docs. Each section gives short principles and the reasoning behind them, with occasional quotes and references to related reading, rather than step-by-step instructions. A note at the start says the lessons are aimed mainly at junior and mid-career developers, with a separate section for leaders. The page text ends partway through the design docs section.
